mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares average power with instantaneous power for a process in which the rate of doing work is not constant?

options.A: Average power is always greater than instantaneous power.
options.B: Average power equals instantaneous power at the instant when the rate of doing work is constant.
options.C: Average power is the derivative of work with respect to time.
options.D: Average power does not depend on the total time interval considered.

mcqs.answer: Average power equals instantaneous power at the instant when the rate of doing work is constant.
mcqs.explanation: Average power is defined as total work done divided by the total time taken (P_avg = W/Δt). Instantaneous power is the instantaneous rate of doing work (P = dW/dt). They are equal only at moments when the rate of doing work is constant, i.e., when dW/dt does not change. The other options misstate the relationship.

mcqs.question: A particle moves along a straight line under a force \(F = 6t\) N, where \(t\) is in seconds. At \(t = 2\) s its velocity is \(4\) m/s. What is the instantaneous power of the force on the particle at \(t = 2\) s?
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power is given by \(P = F \cdot v\). At \(t = 2\) s, \(F = 6 \times 2 = 12\) N and \(v = 4\) m/s, so \(P = 12 \times 4 = 48\) W. Options A, C, and D result from incorrect multiplication.

mcqs.question: A motor does 500 J of work in 10 s. What is the power delivered by the motor?
mcqs.explanation: Power = Work / Time = 500 J / 10 s = 50 W. The other options arise from arithmetic errors.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: Which of the following expressions correctly relates mechanical power to the applied force and the velocity of the point of application?
mcqs.explanation: Mechanical power is the scalar product of force and velocity: \(P = \vec{F}\cdot\vec{v}\). Option B mixes acceleration, C mixes mass, and D mixes displacement, none of which give power.

mcqs.question: Which statement gives the correct definition of average power and distinguishes it from work?

options.A: Average power is the work done divided by the time interval over which the work is done.
options.B: Average power is the total force applied divided by the distance moved.
options.C: Average power is the same as work but expressed in watts.
options.D: Average power is the change in kinetic energy per unit displacement.

mcqs.answer: Average power is the work done divided by the time interval over which the work is done.
mcqs.explanation: Average power \(P_{avg}=W/\Delta t\) quantifies how quickly work is performed. It is not a force‑distance ratio (B), not identical to work (C), and not related to kinetic energy per displacement (D).

mcqs.question: A car engine exerts a constant force of 2000 N on the car and the car moves at a constant speed of 20 m/s on a level road. What is the instantaneous power delivered by the engine?
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power \(P = F \times v = 2000\,\text{N} \times 20\,\text{m/s} = 40,000\,\text{W} = 4.0 \times 10^4\,\text{W}\). Options A, B, and D result from incorrect multiplication or misplaced decimal.

mcqs.question: A crane lifts a 500 kg load vertically through a height of 12 m in 6 s at constant speed. What is the average power output of the crane?
mcqs.explanation: Work done = mgh = 500 kg × 9.8 m/s² × 12 m = 58,800 J. Average power = Work / time = 58,800 J / 6 s = 9,800 W = 9.8 kW. The other options are the result of arithmetic mistakes.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: A cyclist applies a constant pedaling force of 150 N and maintains a speed of 5 m/s on a level road. What is the mechanical power delivered by the cyclist?
mcqs.explanation: Power = Force × Velocity = 150 N × 5 m/s = 750 W. Option A uses half the force, C doubles the result, and D is far too low.
